answer: In PoA, trust propagates through a bounded-length random walk on the attestation graph, with transition mass discounted across edges. A Sybil cluster forms a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits escape probability, while min-cut transitivity bounds the stationary mass it can receive from honest anchors. Therefore, its aggregate voting weight remains constrained: even a haven, pulse, or reef of colluders cannot amplify trust beyond the spectral bound.
